stem:
A cuboidal block floats in a liquid with its base horizontal, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The base of the block is at a depth *h* below the surface of the liquid.

The block is displaced downwards by a small distance and then released so that it oscillates.

Fig. 5.2 shows the variation with *h* of the acceleration *a* of the block.

[[fig:f2]]

Fig. 5.3 shows the variation with *h* of the kinetic energy *E*ₖ of the block.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Determine the amplitude of the oscillations.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State what the line in Fig. 5.2 shows about the nature of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State three other quantitative conclusions that can be drawn from Fig. 5.2 and Fig. 5.3 about the block and its oscillations. Use the space for any working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.4, sketch the variation with *h* of the potential energy *E*ₚ of the oscillations.

[[fig:f4]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A cuboidal block floats in a liquid, with its base below the liquid surface at a depth labelled h.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of acceleration a against depth h shows a straight line decreasing from about 1.0 m s⁻² at h = 0.8 m to −1.0 m s⁻² at h = 2.0 m.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: A graph of kinetic energy Eₖ against depth h shows a downward-opening curve from zero at h = 0.8 m to zero at h = 2.0 m, with a maximum near 1.4 m.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.4
figures.alt: An empty graph grid for sketching potential energy Eₚ against depth h.
